facts.statement: Montanoceratops was a small, quadrupedal herbivore that grew up to 2.5 meters in length and weighed 170 kilograms.
facts.quote: Montanoceratops was a small sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 2.5 m in length and 170 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Montanoceratops were discovered on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Montana within the St. Mary River Formation.
facts.quote: The first fossil remains of what we now know as Montanoceratops were discovered on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation, west of Buffalo Lake, Montana in the St. Mary River Formation.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown and Peter C. Kaisen collected the first Montanoceratops fossils in 1916 from Maastrichtian-aged sediments.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1916 by Barnum Brown and Peter C. Kaisen of the American Museum of Natural History from terrestrial sediments that were deposited during the Maastrichtian stages of the Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer originally named the species Leptoceratops cerorhynchus in 1942 before it was reclassified as Montanoceratops.
facts.quote: After having mounted a reconstruction in 1935, Brown and his assistant Erich Maren Schlaikjer named it in 1942 as a new species of Leptoceratops: Leptoceratops cerorhynchus, later the type species of Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: David B. Weishampel discovered additional Montanoceratops material in 1986 in Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: In 1986, David B. Weishampel discovered more material referable to Montanoceratops in the Little Rocky Coulee locality of the St. Mary River Formation, in Glacier County, Montana.

facts.statement: Peter Makovicky described a well-preserved braincase assigned to Montanoceratops in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001, Peter Makovicky examined and described specimen AMNH 5244, an incomplete but well-preserved braincase that he assigned to Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops was a primitive ceratopsian distinguished by having claws instead of hooves and teeth in its upper jaw instead of a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Montanoceratops was a typical primitive ceratopsian in many respects, distinguished from the later species by the presence of claws, rather than hooves, and by having teeth in its upper jaw, rather than a toothless beak.

facts.statement: Brown and Schlaikjer (1935) noted that Montanoceratops has a large, deep nasal bone with a well-developed horncore and a long dentary with a straight ventral margin.
facts.quote: According to Brown and Schlaikjer (1935), Montanoceratops can be distinguished based on the following characteristics: the nasal bone is proportionally large, deep, heavy and with a very well developed horncore the dentary is long with a straight ventral margin

facts.statement: Charles Mortram Sternberg established the genus Montanoceratops in 1951 after determining the type material was distinct from Leptoceratops.
facts.quote: In 1951, Charles Mortram Sternberg examined more material belonging to Leptoceratops which showed that AMNH 5464 was a distinct genus, and hence he reassigned it to a new genus Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: Chinnery and Weishampel (1996) identified Montanoceratops as the most advanced basal neoceratopsian after finding Protoceratopsidae to be polyphyletic.
facts.quote: In 1996, Chinnery and Weishampel conducted a phylogenetic analysis of basal neoceratopsians which showed that Protoceratopsidae was a polyphyletic group and designated Montanoceratops as the most advanced basal neoceratopsian.

facts.statement: Makovicky (2001) placed Montanoceratops in the taxon Leptoceratopsidae, defined as species closer to Leptoceratops than to Triceratops horridus.
facts.quote: In 2001, Mackovicky, concluded that Montanoceratops belonged to the taxon Leptoceratopsidae, and defined this group as consisting of Leptoceratops gracilis and all species closer to Leptoceratops than to Triceratops horridus.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops possessed tall spines on its tail bones that made the tail unusually deep in cross-section, though invisible during life.
facts.quote: An unusual feature was the presence of tall spines on the bones of the tail. Although these would not have been visible during life, they would have made the tail unusually deep in cross-section.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the flexible, deep tail of Montanoceratops may have been used for intra-species signaling.
facts.quote: Since the tail was also highly flexible, it is possible that it was used in intra-species signalling, and that the deep shape made it more visible.

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH 5464 shows evidence of a severe lifetime injury causing ankylosis in the neural spines of several tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: In specimen AMNH 5464, the neural spines of several caudal vertebrae show ankylosis resulting from a severe injury sustained by the individual during its lifetime.

facts.statement: The St. Mary River Formation, where Montanoceratops fossils are found, dates between 74 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: The St. Mary River Formation has not undergone a definitive radiometric dating; however, the available stratigraphic correlation has shown that this formation was laid down between 74 and 66 million years ago during the final regression of the mid-continental Bearpaw Seaway.

facts.statement: The habitat of Montanoceratops included ancient channels, ponds, streams, and floodplains bounded by mountains to the west.
facts.quote: The region where dinosaurs lived was bounded by mountains to the west, and included ancient channels, small freshwater ponds, streams, and floodplains.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops lived in a wet, warm temperate to subtropical climate that experienced a rapid drop in temperature and precipitation near the end of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The area was wet and warm with a temperate to subtropical climate. Just prior to the Campanian–Maastrichtian boundary, the mean annual temperature and precipitation in this region dropped rapidly.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The first remains of Montanoceratops were collected by Barnum Brown in the St. Mary River Formation of Montana, USA, in 1916.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Montanoceratops fueron recolectados por Barnum Brown en la Formación St Mary River de Montana, Estados Unidos, en 1916.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown and his assistant Erich Schlaikjer named the specimen Leptoceratops cerorhynchos in 1942.
facts.quote: Brown y su ayudante, Erich Schlaikjer, denominaron en 1942 al espécimen como Leptoceratops cerorhynchos.

facts.statement: C.M. Sternberg established the genus Montanoceratops after noticing differences between the specimen and Leptoceratops.
facts.quote: C.M. Sternberg se percató de las diferencias con el espécimen de Brown, estableciendo, finalmente, el género Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: The genus name Montanoceratops means "Montana horned face" and is derived from the state of Montana, the discovery site of the holotype, and the Greek words keras (horn) and ops (face).
facts.quote: El nombre del género Montanoceratops, significa "cara con cuernos de Montana", y se deriva del estado de Montana, que es el sitio del descubrimiento del espécimen holotipo y las palabras griegas keras, κερας que significa "cuerno", y ops, ωψ que significa" cara ".

facts.statement: David B. Weishampel discovered additional Montanoceratops material in 1986 at Little Rocky Coulee in the St. Mary River Formation, Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: En 1986, David B. Weishampel descubrió más material relacionado con Montanoceratops en la localidad de Little Rocky Coulee de la Formación St. Mary River, en el condado de Glacier, Montana.

facts.statement: A description of the additional material was published by Brenda Chinnery and Weishampel in 1998.
facts.quote: Una descripción de este material se publicó en un artículo de Brenda Chinnery y Weishampel en 1998.

facts.statement: In 2001, Peter Makovicky examined and described specimen AMNH 5244, an incomplete but well-preserved skull assigned to Montanoceratops.
facts.quote: En 2001, Peter Makovicky examinado y descrito espécimen AMNH 5244, una incompleto pero bien conservada caja craneana que asigna a Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: The genus Montanoceratops was established by Sternberg in 1951.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sternberg, 1951

facts.statement: The species M. cerorhynchos was originally described by Brown & Schlaikjer in 1935.
facts.quote: species_authority: Brown & Schlaikjer 1935

facts.statement: Leptoceratops cerorynchos is a synonym of Montanoceratops cerorhynchos.
facts.quote: synonyms: Leptoceratops cerorynchos (Brown & Schlaikjer, 1942)

facts.statement: Montanoceratops resembled Protoceratops and measured approximately 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Montanoceratops presenta un aspecto similar al de Protoceratops, llegando a medir alrededor de 3 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops was a typical primitive ceratopsian distinguished from later animals by having hoof-like claws and teeth in the upper jaw instead of a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Era un ceratopsiano primitivo típico en muchos aspectos, distinguiéndose de animales posteriores por la presencia de garras similares a cascos, y por tener dientes en su quijada superior, más que un pico desdentado.

facts.statement: An unusual feature was the presence of high dorsal spines on the tail bones.
facts.quote: Una característica inusual era la presencia de espinas dorsales altas en los huesos de la cola.

facts.statement: Because the tail was highly flexible, it may have been used for communication with conspecifics, and its deep cross-section likely made it more visible.
facts.quote: Puesto que la cola era también altamente flexible, es posible que fuera utilizada en la comunicación con sus congéneres, y que la forma profunda la hiciera más visible.

facts.statement: It was once thought to have a nasal horn, but it actually had a misplaced cheek horn.
facts.quote: Alguna vez se pensó que tenía un cuerno en la nariz, pero era un cuerno de mejilla fuera de lugar.

facts.statement: According to Brown and Schlaikjer in 1942, Montanoceratops can be distinguished by a proportionally large, deep, heavy nasal bone with a well-developed core, and a long dentary with a straight ventral margin.
facts.quote: Según Brown y Schlaikjer en 1942, Montanoceratops se puede distinguir en función de las siguientes características, el hueso nasal es proporcionalmente grande, profundo, pesado y con un núcleo muy bien desarrollado, el dentario es largo con un margen ventral recto.

facts.statement: The original type material discovered by Barnum Brown, cataloged as AMNH 5464, included an incomplete skull and jaw with most of the skull missing, a complete series of eleven cervical, twelve dorsal, and eight sacral vertebrae, thirteen complete caudal vertebrae and the centers of two others, several ribs, a complete pelvic girdle except for the right pubis and distal part of the right ischium, both femurs measuring 346 millimeters, the left tibia measuring 355 millimeters, the left perone and astragalus, the second phalanx of digit three, and the non-manual phalanges of the first, third, and fourth digits of the left foot.
facts.quote: El material tipo original descubierto por Barnum Brown, catalogada como AMNH 5464, incluía un cráneo y mandíbula incompletos, con la mayor parte del cráneo ausente, una serie completa de once vértebras cervicales, doce dorsales y ocho sacras, trece vértebras caudales completas y el centro de otras dos, varias costillas, una cintura pélvica completa, excepto el pubis derecho y la parte distal del isquion derecho, ambos fémures de 346 milímetros, la tibia izquierda de 355 milímetros, el peroné izquierdo y el astrágalo izquierdo, la segunda falange del dígito tres y las falanges no manuales del primer, tercer y cuarto dígitos del pie izquierdo.

facts.statement: This specimen is housed in the collection of the American Museum of Natural History in New York City, USA.
facts.quote: Este espécimen se encuentra en la colección del Museo Americano de Historia Natural en la ciudad de Nueva York, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Charles Mortram Sternberg established the genus Montanoceratops in 1951 after reassigning material previously thought to be Leptoceratops.
facts.quote: En 1951, Charles Mortram Sternberg examinó más material perteneciente a Leptoceratops que mostró que AMNH 5464 era un género distinto, y por lo tanto lo reasignó a un nuevo género Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: Makovicky concluded in 2001 that Montanoceratops belongs to the taxon Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: En 2001, Mackovicky, concluyó que Montanoceratops pertenecía al taxón Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Ryan et al. confirmed the classification of Montanoceratops within Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Un estudio de Ryan et al. en 2012 confirmaron esta asignación.

facts.statement: Chinnery and Weishampel designated Montanoceratops as the most advanced basal neoceratopsian in 1996 after finding the group Protoceratopsidae to be polyphyletic.
facts.quote: En 1996, Chinnery y Weishampel realizaron un análisis filogenético de los neoceratopsianos basales que mostró que el "protoceratopsidae" era un grupo polifilético, es decir, no un taxón válido y designó a Montanoceratops como el neoceratopsiano basal más avanzado.

facts.statement: Montanoceratops lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Montanoceratops is Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Montanoceratops is classified in the family Leptoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Leptoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Montanoceratops belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
